subject: Confirm outage interval and proposed remedy — BlueHarbor checkout impact
messages:
From: Alex Kim <alex@blueharbor.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+alerts@blueharbor.com
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Incident: brief blackout during checkout — impact & evidence request

Hi Stephanie,

We observed a short window where checkout requests started failing with 503s between our customers 08:03 and 08:06 PDT this morning. That window coincides with a spike in failed transactions on our side (approx 2.3% of requests over that period). We rely on Redwood for inference during payment authorization; the failures caused ~120 failed checkouts and a small revenue hit for us.

Can you confirm:
- Exact service-unavailable interval as you see it on Redwood's side (start/end with timezones)
- Whether this meets the SLA credit eligibility thresholds and how you calculate the credit
- What logs/bundles you can provide for our auditors (we need request IDs and traces for a sample)

I've attached a short CSV with the affected order IDs and timestamps (blueharbor-impact-summary.csv). Please escalate to reliability if needed — our finance team is already preparing a chargeback request pending confirmation.

Thanks,
Alex Kim
Head of Platform Operations, Blue Harbor Payments
alex@blueharbor.com

--

What we'll provide in the next update:
- Precise start/end times (UTC and PDT) from our edge and control-plane logs
- Request ID samples and KV cache traces for a subset of the failures you sent

Next steps: I've looped in Laura (customer success) to manage the billing conversation and Marcus/Rishi to pull logs and traces. If you have any additional order IDs or spans, please send them now.

Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incident: brief blackout during checkout — impact & evidence request

Thanks — I pulled the relevant control-plane and serving traces. Preliminary findings (short summary):

- Verified outage window: 2025-09-30T15:03:11Z through 2025-09-30T15:05:58Z (UTC) which is 08:03:11 - 08:05:58 PDT.
- Root cause (initial): autoscaler mis-evaluated load spike during a brief GC pause on a pinned node group; result was a short moment of elevated 503s while remaining requests fell back to a cold variant.
- We attached a trace bundle and 20 sample request IDs correlating to the IDs in your CSV: outage_trace_bundle-20250930.tar.gz

SLA credit calculation (per contract DH-4821, section 4.2): monthly uptime < 99.95% => prorated credit. For a 2 minute, 47 second unavailability in us-west over a 30-day period, proposed calculation: (outage_seconds / seconds_in_month) * monthly_fee. Rough estimate for September: outage_seconds = 167s; seconds_in_month = 2592000 => fraction = 6.44e-05.

Proposed immediate remedy:
- Offer a pro-rated credit for the month of September using the calculation above (we'll convert to USD on the invoice).
- Full postmortem with mitigation plan and timeline within 5 business days.
- Optional: a one-time technical review call with our SREs to walk traces and prevention steps.

Drive link to evidence bundle: https://drive.redwood.example/drive/outage-20250930
Attachment: outage_trace_bundle-20250930.tar.gz (log bundle, traces, and reconciled request-id list)

If that credit path looks acceptable to Blue Harbor, Laura can coordinate the invoice adjustment and apply the credit once the numbers are finalized.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
